notes:
Context: Mid-market product analytics vendor building an in-app assistant and enterprise search. Started on Redwood Hosted API for fast iteration; now wants a Dedicated POC to validate latency/cost under sustained traffic and to get an enterprise contract.

POC goals: Validate Dedicated throughput (50–200 req/s bursts), p95 <= 200ms for short responses (<256 tokens), embedding latency <= 150ms for vector generation, unit cost target ~40% lower than hosted list for baseline model.

POC scope and success criteria:
- Canary rollout plan: 2-week POC. Start with 5% traffic to Dedicated for first 24 hours, then 20% for next 48h, then 60% day 6–10, full ramp day 11 if SLOs met.
- Metrics to monitor: p50/p95 latency, token/sec, error rate, tail latency (99.9th), memory pressure, KV cache hit rate, cost per 1k tokens. Auto-rollback if p95 increases >25% vs baseline or error rate >1% sustained for 10m.
- Fallback routing: primary => Dedicated pool in us-east; fallback => Hosted API endpoints (same model variant) plus lightweight model variant (redwood-llama-13b-8bit) for low-latency requests during capacity spikes. Region failover: route to eu-west Dedicated pool if us-east capacity compromised; traffic shift controlled via routing policy with canary + warmup.
- Model variants: baseline = redwood-mix-7b-q4, performance variant = redwood-mix-7b-q4f (faster kernels), quality variant = redwood-13b-8bit for long-form responses. POC will test 7b-q4 for chat and 13b-8bit only for >512 token responses.
- Rollback plan: automated based on metric thresholds (see above) + manual rollback button in Console. If rollback triggers, route 100% traffic back to Hosted API and open incident for SE + infra.
- Security: VPC peering, SSO (SAML), audit logs retention 12 months, KMS integration for key material.

Quotes / call snippets: "We need predictable latency for in-app help — sub-200ms p95 or customers will notice." — Head of Product.
"If Dedicated gives us a consistent 40% cost reduction we can commit to a 12-month reserved pool" — CFO (paraphrase).

Pricing discussion notes: mid-Feb pricing sheet v1 shared (drive:/pricing/dedicated_poc_bludelta_v1.pdf). Customer asked for a bridge pricing for POC (discounted reserved block for 30 days) and an overage cap. SE proposed burst capacity with soft limits and cost alerts.

Operational runbook (high-level):
- Day -3: provide VPC peering diagram + IAM roles, infra to test connectivity.
- Day 0: provision Dedicated pool (2xA10G equiv) in us-east for POC. Load test with synthetic traffic.
- Day 1–2: 5% traffic canary; monitor.
- Day 3–5: 20% traffic; test fallback to hosted on simulated overload.
- Day 6–10: 60% traffic; measure cost and latency under realistic session patterns.
- Day 11–14: Ramp to 100% if SLOs and legal approved. Procurement to finalize contract.

Open technical questions for SE/infra: GPU sizing for 99th percentile, expected token distribution, best quantization profile for embeddings, autoscaling cooldown defaults, estimated KV cache hit rate with 7-day session retention.
